thread:
Carla: Quick sync — several customers are pressing for private deploy with customer-managed networking. Need final launch acceptance criteria and a concise test matrix. Who can take the first pass?

Ben: I'll start a draft. High level thoughts: we need clear allowed topologies, required handoffs (BGP vs SNAT), and deterministic egress behavior. Also list of automated tests.

Ben: Acceptance checklist (draft):
1) BGP session established and stable for 10 minutes with route advertisement verified
2) Egress IP behavior: either pinned public IPs or clearly documented SNAT with TTL for sessions
3) DNS/hostname resolution for endpoints from customer VPC (internal DNS delegation validated)
4) KMS integration end-to-end (encrypt/decrypt, audit log entries present)
5) Failover test: region fallback triggers and model traffic continues within SLO
6) Observability: traces include customer-request-id and token-level cost attribution
7) Security: mutual TLS or customer ACLs validated

Mike: For on-prem/NB: need L2 vs L3 handoff doc. Also asymmetric routing is a real risk — we should have a hard requirement for symmetric path or set expectations that KV cache may not be preserved.

Alice: Product scope note: initially support AWS and GCP private interconnects (Direct Connect / Interconnect) + VPN. BGP-based peering is enterprise-only feature. For GA we should support SNAT and a pinned-egress-IP option. Pricing/packaging needs to reflect the higher operational cost for BGP setups.

Srini: Edge cases to call out in the RFC: overlapping CIDRs (require NAT or route translation), multi-CIDR customers, customers that rotate egress IPs frequently (we should set a cadence and require advance notice), and customers that expect cross-tenant egress IP reuse (disallow unless isolated).

Kate: From support POV: add these acceptance tests:
- customer-run: curl from their VPC to health endpoint and validate 200 + expected headers (x-redwood-region, x-request-id)
- DNS epoch test: customer updates DNS record and we verify propagation within agreed TTL
Also we need a runbook with rollback steps and escalation contact matrix.

Ben: Sample health check command we should document for customers to run:
```
curl -v -H 'Host: models.redwood.internal' http://10.0.0.5/health
```
Expect 200 and header `x-redwood-instance` present.

Ben: For testing we propose three automated suites:
- Network handshake suite: BGP session, route advertisement, DNS delegation tests
- E2E inference suite: start small model (seq=256) and measure latency/throughput under baseline load (1k rps)
- Chaos/network resilience suite: simulate BGP withdrawal, packet loss, and validate fallback policies

Mike: Eng-infra can own the BGP simulator and chaos harness. Rough estimate: 2 sprints to stand up a realistic BGP simulator + 1 sprint to integrate tests. Need org-level prioritization.

devops-bot: Draft checklist created and attached to PRD stub: https://internal.redwood/prd/private-deploy-networking (internal link).

Carla: Ok action items (agree or object):
1) Ben: write RFC with concrete acceptance criteria + test matrix and include the sample curl + config examples — due EOD Friday (1965530000).
2) Mike: spin up BGP simulator spike Monday and share ETA in #eng-infra.
3) Alice: finalize supported topologies and pricing note (mark BGP as enterprise add-on).
4) Kate: draft support runbook and rollback procedures.
Please reply with any objections. Tagging @Ben @Mike @Alice @Kate @Srini :thumbsup:
